summary: Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Mahidol University by 2021, supervised by Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto, alongside several other teachers.
Enga Teramoto (1872–1940) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Kyoto University around 1908 and as a professor at Otani University from 1915.
Enichi Ocho (1906–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1926 to 1929. He later served as professor emeritus at Otani University (attested 1972–1979).

Enryo Inoue (1858–1919) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Higashi Hongan-ji, Nagaoka High School, and the University of Tokyo (~1881–1885). He founded Toyo University and held a post there (~1887–1919).

Ensho Kanakura (1896–1987) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1917–1920). A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he was professor at Tohoku University (~1926–1959), professor at Rissho University (~1958–1974), and president of Miyagi University of Education (~1967–1974).
Ensho Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University (attested 1996) under the supervision of Eshō Mikogami.

Enshu Kurumiya (b. 1942) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from the Australian National University in 1974 and served as professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).

Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) was a Tibetologist and historian who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 1981. He lectured at the University of Milan (attested 1996) and held a post at the University of Bologna (~2002).

Eric David Mortensen works in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003), where he was supervised by Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton.
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) studied at the University of Manchester (~1955–1958) and worked in religious studies and Indology. He held posts at Manchester (~1966–1970), Lancaster (~1970–1977), and the University of Sydney as First Chair of Religious Studies (1977–1996).

Eric M. Greene works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (2012) under Robert H. Sharf and was appointed assistant professor of religious studies at Yale University (attested 2017).
Eric Reinders works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell.

Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MA at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and studied at the University of Virginia (attested 2012) under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

Erich Frauwallner (1898–1974) was an Austrian scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Vienna (1918–1921). He later served there as professor extraordinarius (1955), professor (1960–1963), and professor emeritus (~1968–1974).

Erich Haenisch (1880–1966) was a scholar of Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held professorships at Leipzig University (~1925–1932), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1945), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1946–1952), among other posts.
Erich Rudolf Jaensch (1883–1940) was a scholar in philosophy and other fields. He held academic posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1910–1913) and the University of Marburg (~1913–1940).
Erik Braun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University, where his doctoral supervisor was Janet Gyatso.

Erik Haarh (1929–1993) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He earned a doctor's degree at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1969) and held a post at the Royal Danish Library from around 1957 to 1974.
Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from Indiana University and served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).
